title: Two-Stage Ordering Kinetics in Binary Mixtures of Ellipsoidal Particles
authors: Parameshwaran A, Sanjay Puri, Bhaskar Sen Gupta
abstract: We investigate the nonequilibrium phase-ordering kinetics of a binary mixture of uniaxial ellipsoidal particles interacting via the anisotropic Gay-Berne potential using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Following a temperature quench from the isotropic and homogeneous phase into the coexistence region, the system exhibits two distinct ordering processes occurring on different time scales. At first, rapid orientational ordering leads to the formation and coarsening of nematic domains, characterized by dynamical scaling, generalized Porod-law behavior, and a growth law $\ell(t) \sim t^{1/2}$ consistent with nonconserved order-parameter dynamics. Later, the system undergoes binary phase separation driven by compositional fluctuations. This compositional ordering process shows a transition from diffusive growth $\ell(t) \sim t^{1/3}$ to hydrodynamic regimes, with finite-size scaling analysis indicating asymptotic viscous growth $\ell(t) \sim t$. Despite the presence of global orientational order, the phase-separation kinetics remains effectively isotropic. These results demonstrate a clear separation between orientational and compositional ordering dynamics, governed by distinct conservation laws, and provide a unified framework for understanding phase ordering in anisotropic particle systems.
summary: This work uses molecular dynamics simulations to study how binary mixtures of anisotropic ellipsoids order over time. It reveals a two-stage process: first, rapid alignment into nematic domains, followed by slower compositional phase separation. The study successfully distinguishes the characteristic growth laws for each process, demonstrating that these ordering mechanisms can proceed sequentially without significantly interfering with each other's large-scale dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates the nonequilibrium phase-ordering kinetics in a binary mixture of anisotropic ellipsoidal particles, specifically focusing on the separation between orientational and compositional ordering processes.
main_result: The system exhibits two distinct, sequential ordering processes: rapid orientational ordering ($\ell(t) \sim t^{1/2}$) followed by slower compositional phase separation ($\ell(t) \sim t^{1/3}$ transitioning to $\ell(t) \sim t$).
method: Large-scale Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations were employed, supplemented by dynamical scaling and finite-size scaling analyses to characterize the time evolution of domain sizes.
model_or_system: The system models a binary mixture of uniaxial ellipsoidal particles interacting via the anisotropic Gay-Berne potential. The simulation involves quenching the system from an isotropic state into the coexistence region.
key_observables: Domain size $\ell(t)$, nematic order parameter $S_G$, two-point correlation function $C(r, t)$, and structure factor $S(k, t)$.
important_parameters: Temperature quench from $T=6.0$ to $T=2.3$; anisotropy parameters ($\kappa, \kappa'$); and the resulting growth exponents ($\alpha=1/2$ and $\alpha=1$).
main_assumptions: The late-time growth exponent $\alpha=1$ for phase separation is attributed to viscous hydrodynamic effects, and deviations from scaling are due to finite-size effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Gay-Berne potential, phase diagrams showing transitions (I $ightarrow$ Nm $ightarrow$ Sm), and time evolution of domain sizes $\ell(t)$ exhibiting power-law growth in different regimes.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and simulation setup, then analyzes the distinct time scales of orientational ordering (nematic domain formation) and compositional ordering (phase separation), concluding with a unified framework showing their sequential, yet decoupled, dynamics.
why_interesting: The clear separation of dynamics into distinct power-law regimes ($\ell(t) \sim t^{1/2}$ vs $\ell(t) \sim t$) provides a powerful, generalized framework for understanding how multiple order parameters evolve sequentially in complex, anisotropic many-body systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Representative form of the GB interaction potential illustrating the anisotropic dependence of the interaction energy on intermolecular separation and relative orientation. The potential exhibits distinct well depths for side-by-side and end-to-end configurations, reflecting the underlying energy anisotropy of ellipsoidal particles.

FIG. 4: Radial distribution function g(r) for different phases. The smectic phase exhibits pronounced oscillations due to layered compositional ordering, whereas the nematic phase shows rapidly damped oscillations, indicating short-range compositional correlations.

FIG. 2: Variation of the average potential energy per particle, ⟨Epe⟩, as a function of temperature T for the GB model system. The discontinuities in the curve mark the isotropic-nematic and nematic-smectic phase transitions.

FIG. 3: Representative configurations of the GB system in different equilibrium phases: isotropic (disordered orientations), nematic (long-range orientational order), and smectic (layered structure with partial compositional order).

FIG. 5: Time evolution of orientational ordering following a temperature quench from the isotropic phase (T = 6.0) to the nematic phase (T = 2.3). The snapshots show the progressive emergence, growth, and coalescence of nematic domains. For clarity, only a 203 subvolume taken from one corner of the full simulation box is displayed.
